name: Kunphan
why_it_matters: Sit-down restaurant inside Hotel Ladakh House on the Upper Pelling road, with a glass-wrapped dining room that opens onto Pandim and Kanchenjunga on a clear morning. One of the few places in Pelling cooking thenthuk and Tibetan noodle work to standard, not Indian-Chinese substitutes.
insider_tip: Order 20 minutes before you arrive if you can — kitchen is small and dishes are made to order. Skip the continental section and stick to the Tibetan-Sikkimese menu.
signature_address: Hotel Ladakh House, Upper Pelling, near Sky Walk, West Sikkim 737113

name: Hotel Kabur Restaurant
why_it_matters: Hotel Kabur was one of Pelling's first hotels and the in-house kitchen, run by Chef Teshi Gurung's family, has stayed on Sikkimese cooking when everyone else pivoted to Indian-Chinese for tour buses. Wood-panelled dining room with ridge views; reliable for ved-thenduk and proper pork momos.
insider_tip: Sikkimese menu is on a separate sheet — ask for it. The standard Indian Chinese menu is fine but doesn't show what the kitchen actually does well.
signature_address: Main Pelling road, near Helipad, West Sikkim 737113

name: Mama's Kitchen
why_it_matters: Family-run kitchen attached to the homestay of the same name — Pema and her parents cook everything from scratch in an open kitchen guests can sit in. Bread is baked daily; vegetables come from the family plot above the village. Common dinner stop for trekkers descending from Dzongri-Goecha La.
insider_tip: Order at least an hour ahead, especially the thali — Pema works alone most evenings. Wood-fired bread is best at breakfast straight from the oven.
signature_address: Main road, Yuksom Bazaar, West Sikkim 737113

name: Traditional Inn
why_it_matters: A four-table joint in Yuksom Bazaar where the noodles for thenthuk are rolled and pulled by the owner's mother and grandmother in the kitchen behind the dining bench. Non-spicy by default — Sikkimese-Bhutanese style — with a separate spicy chutney plate brought on request. The handmade-noodle test most Sikkim 'Tibetan' restaurants fail.
insider_tip: Lunch is the noodle window — they roll fresh dough between 11am and 2pm. Phagshapa pork sells out by 1pm on busy days.

name: Limboo Homestay Kitchen
why_it_matters: Open to non-staying guests on advance booking — the family cooks Limbu Sikkimese plates that don't appear in restaurant kitchens, including yangben (a lichen-based curry) and home-fermented tongba poured into bamboo cylinders. Vegetables come from the family's organic plot.
insider_tip: Call a day ahead to book lunch or dinner — kitchen only cooks for confirmed numbers. Tongba is poured continuously, hot water added; one cylinder is enough for two.

name: Roots and Shoots
signature_dish: Niguro (fern shoots) with churpi and gorkhey chutney
why_it_matters: Farm-to-table from the family's certified-organic farm — fern shoots, churpi cheese, gundruk and most herbs come in the morning of service. The name refers to the literal contents of Sikkimese village cooking: roots, shoots, ferns. Ranks #4 among Ravangla's Tripadvisor restaurants but #1 for actual Sikkimese plates.
insider_tip: The niguro-churpi only runs March-October when ferns are in season. In winter ask for the buckwheat-based phaapar dishes instead.
signature_address: Kewzing Road, opposite Power Colony, near Hotel Ravongla Star, Ravangla 737139

name: Tathagata Kitchen
signature_dish: Sikkimese thali with phagshapa and gundruk
why_it_matters: Named after the Tathagata Tsal (Buddha Park) two minutes up the road. Built around a proper Sikkimese thali rather than the hotel-Indian default. Wood interiors with traditional Sikkimese textiles. 4.4/5 on Tripadvisor across 16 reviews.
insider_tip: The thali is the order — three curries, gundruk, dal, rice and a sweet, with phagshapa swapped in for vegetarians. Avoid the pizza section.
signature_address: Main Ravangla bazaar, near Mane Choekhorling Gompa, South Sikkim 737139

name: Read & Feed Cafe
why_it_matters: Small books-and-coffee cafe with garden seating onto the valley below Ravangla bazaar. Coffee is sourced from Sikkimese small-holder estates rather than the standard South Indian filter blend. Decent place to wait out the post-lunch monastery-tour rush.
insider_tip: Garden seats fill up by 11am on weekends — the upstairs reading room with the Sikkim history shelf usually has space.

name: Flavours Restaurant
signature_dish: Pork momos with house chilli paste
why_it_matters: Owner Smita Rai runs a tight kitchen and a stocked bar in a town where most restaurants close by 9pm. The pork momos draw repeat customers driving up from Siliguri; reviewers consistently rank them above the Darjeeling-Kalimpong belt's better-known momo houses. Karaoke runs Friday-Saturday evenings.
insider_tip: Sit downstairs near the kitchen — the bar level fills with a karaoke crowd after 8pm. Pork comes from Bhutia farms in the surrounding villages.
signature_address: Near Bhanu Stadium, Namchi, South Sikkim 737126

name: Crumbs N' Whips Cafe Bistro & Grill
why_it_matters: The only proper espresso-bar setup in Namchi — Naya Bazar storefront with an in-house bakery turning out cinnamon rolls and brownies daily. Wide spaced seating that fits families, which the typical hill-town cafe doesn't. Pasta and pizza are cooked to order, not microwaved.
insider_tip: Pastries are best in the morning straight out of the oven; afternoon coffee usually comes with a 20-minute wait once the post-Char Dham crowd hits.
signature_address: Namchi-Naya Bazar Road, Namchi, South Sikkim 737126

name: Adonai Family Restaurant
why_it_matters: Family-run multi-cuisine in Lal Bazaar with an attached coffee corner. Sit-down meals lean Chinese-Continental; the coffee operation runs separately and is one of two places in Namchi serving freshly brewed coffee with consistency.
insider_tip: Coffee corner opens earlier than the main restaurant — useful before 9am when the kitchen's still warming up.
signature_address: Lal Bazaar, Agam Gram, Namchi, South Sikkim 737126
